text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Businessman fined 25,000 after being convicted of insider trading in shares of car suspension maker Weweler. (p1).
- Publisher Wegener Arcade 1996 net profit up 16 pct at NLG 68 million; company expects further profit growth. (p1)
- Robeco Group of investment funds sees net assets rise sharply in 1996; expects lower return on shares in 1997. (p1)
- Top official at Dutch ministry of economic affairs says European economy would benefit more from divergent economic policies among member states rather than harmonisation. (p1)
- Publisher Reed Elsevier reveals ambitious plans for major science database. (p3)
- Real estate broker DTZ Zadelhoff sees Dutch office rents rising by about ten percent. (p3)
- Delfzijl in northern province Groningen is lobbying for a second port in Eemshaven. (p3)
- Wholesalers in computers, office equipment and furniture see 1996 Q3 turnover rise 18.5 pct compared to Q3 of 1995. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Russia's president Boris Yeltsin to visit The Hague on February 4 for talks with prime minister Wim Kok and European Commission president Jacques Santer. (p1)
- Eleven Cities ice-skating competition held in Friesland province Friesland on Saturday was a popular success. (p2)
- Mobile phones used intensively during Eleven Cities skating race, say operators PTT Telecom and Libertel (p3).
- Chinese Mors motorbikes to be launched on Dutch market soon. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- A record 9.2 million people watched at least part of the Eleven Cities skating competition on television. (p3)
- Cabinet to decide in March on possible bourse flotation of Amsterdam's Schiphol airport. (p13)
- KLM Royal Dutch Airlines cargo unit is poised for further growth. (p13)
- Port towing firms in nine North Sea ports between Hamburg and Le Havre face falling demand for their services. (p13)
TROUW
- FNV trade union federation drops principle of equal pay for same work; no says higher levels of education and training should result in higher wages. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- PTT Telecom complains that many mobile phone users are slow to pay their bills. (p3)
